Container.Name: pocket-dev
Container.Overview:
Browser-accessible terminal for Claude Code, mobile-first. Spawns a tmux session running Claude under a restart loop and exposes it via xterm.js over WebSocket, so a desktop or phone can attach to the same session and survive disconnects.
Click the WebUI button to open the terminal in your browser. Claude auto-starts; just begin typing.
Authentication: provide ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or run 'claude login' once. Auth persists in the config volume.

Config.Name: Lavish Editor Port
Config.Description: Lavish Editor review server. A session runs `lavish-axi <file.html>`, which prints a URL you open on a phone or desktop to annotate the artifact and send feedback back to the agent. The server binds the container's own IP (entrypoint.sh resolves it; 0.0.0.0 is refused by Lavish and coerced to loopback), so this mapping is what makes the URL reachable at all. It serves the artifact and its local assets WITHOUT authentication, so treat it like the terminal port above: only publish it on a network you trust. The number is the web terminal port plus one, so there is one port to remember rather than two.

Config.Name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Config.Description: Optional: Your Anthropic API key. If not provided, run 'claude login' in the terminal on first use.

Config.Name: Workspace
Config.Description: Directory where claude-code will work with your files

Config.Name: Home
Config.Description: The container's entire home directory, and the only state mount you need. Everything a tool writes to ~ persists across image updates: Claude's config and conversation ids, the gh auth token, the dgvpn registration, and credentials for tools that were never on this list (aws, kubectl, fly, docker). This REPLACED a separate mount per dotfile; anything the old list forgot silently evaporated on every recreate. The image keeps its own artifacts in /opt/pd-home and ships this path empty, which is what makes mounting the whole home safe. Must be owned 99:100 (nobody:users) on the host, or the server disables its session store silently and tabs stop coming back.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Docker socket. WARNING: Mode=ro does NOT make the Docker API read-only. It marks the socket file read-only and nothing more; the daemon still accepts every write call (run, stop, rm) over it, verified on a live container. Anything in here can therefore start a privileged container and take over the host, so treat this mount as host root. Remove it, or put a filtered docker-socket-proxy in front of it, if that is not what you want.

Config.Name: DGVPN_PROXY_PORT
Config.Description: Local port for the dgvpn userspace CONNECT proxy.

Config.Name: DGVPN_DIR
Config.Description: Where dgvpn keeps its tsnet registration. Inside the Home mount, so the ~24h Keycloak auth survives a recreate with no volume of its own.

Config.Name: LAVISH_AXI_LINK_HOST
Config.Description: The hostname YOU reach this container by, written into the review URLs Lavish prints. Leave it blank and the URL carries the container's 172.x bridge address, which resolves nowhere outside the container: the feature looks broken while working perfectly. Set it to a name or address that reaches the Docker host, e.g. its LAN IP or its Tailscale MagicDNS name. Setting it also adds that name to Lavish's Host allowlist, so no matching entry in LAVISH_AXI_ALLOWED_HOSTS is needed.

Config.Name: LAVISH_AXI_ALLOWED_HOSTS
Config.Description: Extra Host header values Lavish answers to, whitespace-separated. Its DNS-rebinding guard 403s anything that is not loopback, the bind address, or LAVISH_AXI_LINK_HOST, and answers with a page naming the URL that does work. Add the OTHER names you might type for this host (LAN IP, short hostname, Tailscale IP) so those do not 403. A lone `*` disables the guard entirely; only do that behind your own authentication.

Config.Name: SHELL_CMD
Config.Description: Override the command each session runs instead of Claude. Leave EMPTY for normal use. A non-empty value silently disables conversation resume, because a custom command is not necessarily Claude and has no transcript to resume (see RESUME_ENABLED in server.js). Mainly for testing; the e2e suite sets it to cat.
